title: Patchwork regression hypotheses — mini scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
A compact, messy log of small regression signals I saw in the hosted-api outputs this week. Not a formal postmortem — just an actionable patchwork of hypotheses and quick tests to triage whether this is model drift, prompt-surface regression, or runtime-level quantization/kv-cache fallout.

Background snapshot:
- Surface: hosted-api, chat.complete endpoint, model pinned to open-7B-v2 (customer sandbox)
- Trigger time window: 2024-10-25 -> 2024-10-27 (spike of user reports + internal QA sampling)
- Observed symptom: increase in short-answer hallucinations for factoid questions (entities/dates) and occasional truncation mid-sentence at ~token 120–130
- Baseline: checks on 2024-10-20 samples looked fine (low hallucination rate for same prompts)

Quick summary of representative examples (redacted):
1) Prompt: "When was the Osborne Act enacted?"
   - Baseline output (10/20): "The Osborne Act was enacted in 1989." (accurate; customer dataset says 1989)
   - Anomalous output (10/26): "It was enacted in 1991."
   - Notes: low-confidence phrasing (no citation), single-token difference but repeated across 3 seeds

2) Prompt: "Summarize the policy changes in PR-47" (internal PR title)
   - Baseline: concise 4-line summary focusing on auth behavior
   - Anomaly: dropped third bullet and appended generic guidance, output ended abruptly with "...and should be" (truncated)

3) Prompt: short chat instruction -> model emits repeated phrase "Please clarify the question." twice; appears correlated with messages that include a trailing whitespace/newline in user content

Mini ad-hoc rubric (for quick scoring):
- Hallucination severity: 0 (none), 1 (minor factual mismatch), 2 (plausible wrong assertion), 3 (obviously wrong/confident)
- Fluency/truncation: 0 (clean), 1 (minor pause/odd token), 2 (incomplete sentence), 3 (mid-sentence stop/truncated)
- Repetition/guardrail: 0 (no repeat), 1 (1 repetition), 2 (pattern repeated), 3 (looping)

Apply rubric to samples above:
- Example 1: hallucination=1, fluency=0, repetition=0
- Example 2: hallucination=2? (loss of coverage), fluency=3 (truncation), repetition=0
- Example 3: hallucination=0, fluency=1, repetition=2

Initial hypotheses (prioritized):
A) Model roll (version/weights swap) or checkpoint mismatch. Small changes to tokenization or a newer variant could shift probabilities for low-frequency entities.
B) Runtime quantization / kernel change introduced a subtle bias at token ~120 due to KV cache mis-management on some hardware. Truncation patterns line up with token window boundary behavior in the runtime.
C) Prompt normalization change in the API (trimming vs keeping trailing whitespace/newline) leading to different context framing, explaining the repeated guardrail message on whitespace inputs.
D) Sampling parameter default tweak (temperature/top_k) pushed during autoscaling config change for some customer tiers.

Quick checks to run (cheap, 1–2 hours):
1) Re-run exact failing prompts locally against pinned model commit hash from 10/20 vs current pinned hash. Compare top-k token distributions for the differing step(s). (linked PR/commit IDs above)
2) Force-run requests with/without trailing newline via curl to see if the double-"Please clarify" reproduces (isolates prompt normalization hypothesis C).
3) Produce token-level log (non-prod) on the hosted node that gave a truncated response. Correlate truncation token index with runtime logs: gc/evict events, kv-cache resize, batch boundary.
4) Spin up same model on a single dedicated GPU (dedicated pool) with identical runtime flags to rule out autoscaler-per-queue behavior.

Small experiments to prioritize now:
- A: Compare outputs with quantized vs fp16 variants (cheap if available) to check for distribution shifts.
- B: Replay with deterministic sampling (temperature=0, top_p=1) to see whether hallucination persists (if it does, suggests model weights rather than sampling).
- C: Run a small sweep toggling 'trim_whitespace' flag to see if repetition drops off.

Data & instrumentation notes (what we have / need):
- We have telemetry for end-to-end token counts and error traces but limited token-level logits saved (costly).
- Need at least one reproduction trace with token logits for ~50 failing requests to analyze argmax dynamics.
- Add a transient flag to save token streams for a single customer sandbox for 24h.

Customer impact & risk assessment:
- A few sandbox customers reported wrong dates in downstream UI; not yet production-critical but will erode trust if frequency increases.
- Truncation is higher risk: if it affects summary endpoints, users may miss critical info.

What to surface to product/ops now:
- Short note in #cs-incidents with a couple of redacted examples and request to hold on any model rollouts for the affected model family until we triage.
- Ask SRE to snapshot one hosted node logset for the time window where truncation spikes observed (10/26 14:00–16:00 UTC).

Open questions (quick):
- Any scheduled runtime/kernel updates around 10/24–10/26? (release-engineering has a deployment note?)
- Was there a change to default sampling config for burst queues? (platform-engineering)
- Are there known tokenization changes between open-7B-v2 commits in late Oct? (applied-ml / model-onboarding)

Next actions (me / 48h):
- Marcos: run deterministic replay for 20 failing prompts (today) and save token traces for the 3 most representative failures.
- Asha: toggle whitespace trimming flag on a staging proxy and run the short reproducibility sweep (24h).
- Naya: coordinate with SRE for node log snapshot and to confirm any infra changes during the window.

Notes-to-self / heuristics observed (informal):
- Truncation events often cluster near ~128 tokens in these samples — suspect boundary artifact.
- Repetition often correlates with inputs that have trailing newlines or accidental carriage returns from copy/paste — quick mitigation: normalize incoming text at API layer (preserve but also provide a sanitized version to model?).
- Small fact flips tend to be single-token edits (years, IDs) — check tokenization map: those years might be split into different token sequences across commits.

If this morphs into a larger pattern: prepare a short automated eval harness (100 prompts, golden answers) and track daily pass rate; tie to alert if failure rate > 3% for two consecutive days.

Random scratch ideas (for later):
- Lightweight "confidence delta" metric: compute token-level entropy shift between baseline and current; surface the top 5 tokens with largest delta for each failure to get quick signal.
- Use forced-decode (temperature=0) snapshots to detect whether top-1 changed vs top-5 distribution wideness (helps separate sampling vs model change).

End quick patchwork notes.

-- Marcos
(throwaway scratchpad: keep short, circle back with formal writeup if we find a reproducible root cause)
